The General Fund closed at revenues of $193,943,997 against expenditures of $191,501,331 — a surplus of $2,442,666, some $1,642,407 better than the $800,259 budgeted at the final amendment. https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
What it is
The year-end unaudited statement of revenues and expenditures for fiscal 2023-24, presented August 20, 2024. Uniquely among the monthly statements it carries a variance column showing dollar and percentage differences against the 6/20/24 final amended budget.

General Fund — the year's result
- Revenues $193,943,997 against $193,048,749 budgeted, **+$895,248 (+0.46%)** — Local $44,384,530 (-$103,289); State $128,437,252 (-$105,397); Federal $8,182,483 (+$282,045); **Interdistrict $12,939,732 (+$821,889, +6.78%)**
- Expenditures $191,501,331 against $192,248,490, **-$674,404 (-0.35%)** — Instruction $124,937,442 (-$732,523); Support Services $65,808,973 (+$42,013)
- **Revenues over expenditures $2,442,666 against a budgeted $800,259 — better by $1,642,407**

Where the variance came from
On the expenditure side the swing is concentrated: Added Needs $30,387,177 came in **$1,450,839 (4.56%) under budget**, and Adult Education $866,055 was $102,507 (10.58%) under. Against that, Basic Programs ran $820,823 over at $93,684,210, Operations $292,052 over at $14,402,712, and General Administration $210,639 (8.69%) over at $2,635,585. Community Services overran by 10.95% and Debt Service underran by the same 10.95%.

On the revenue side, interdistrict sources — the PA-18 special education distribution from Oakland Schools — beat budget by $821,889, more than offsetting the small local and state shortfalls.

Other funds at year-end
Debt Service: revenues $31,044,282 against expenditures of $30,849,637, essentially exactly on budget, surplus $194,645. Food Service: revenues $6,655,436 against $6,204,141, surplus $451,295 — federal revenue of $2,023,290 beat its $1,679,000 budget by 21%. Troy Career Center: revenues $2,660,276 against expenditures $2,606,552 — a $53,724 surplus, the first time the fund has not closed at exactly zero. Community Service: revenues $1,963,869 against expenditures $2,190,377, deficit $(226,508) against a budgeted $(131,071). Preschool: revenues $4,177,298 against $3,770,339, surplus $406,959.

Capital funds — the underspend that shaped the next year
2023 Capital Projects: revenue $10,180,060 against expenditures of $17,049,404 — capital outlay $16,854,191 of a $65,327,399 budget, only **26%**. The $48 million left unspent is what restated the following year's opening balance to $133,553,267. Sinking Fund: revenue $4,892,082 against capital outlay $7,323,438 — 126% of its $5,800,000 budget — a $(2,431,356) draw against a budgeted $(925,000). 2019 Capital Projects: revenue $77,114, capital outlay $648,619 against a $486,200 budget.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
This is Troy School District's year-end unaudited statement of revenues and expenditures for fiscal 2023-24, covering the year ended June 30, 2024 and presented to the Board on August 20, 2024. It is the most informative of the monthly series because it alone carries a variance column comparing actual results against the 6/20/24 final amended budget in both dollars and percentages.

General Fund revenues total $193,943,997 against $193,048,749 budgeted — a favourable variance of $895,248, or 0.46%. By source: Local Sources $44,384,530 against $44,487,819, short by $103,289 or 0.23%; State Sources $128,437,252 against $128,542,649, short by $105,397 or 0.08%; Federal Sources $8,182,483 against $7,900,438, over by $282,045 or 3.57%; and Interdistrict Sources $12,939,732 against $12,117,843, over by $821,889 or 6.78%. The interdistrict overage — the PA-18 special education distribution flowing from Oakland Schools — is the single largest favourable revenue variance and more than covers the small local and state shortfalls.

General Fund expenditures total $191,501,331 against $192,248,490 budgeted, a favourable variance of $674,404 or 0.35%. Instruction totals $124,937,442 against $125,669,965, under by $732,523 or 0.58%: Basic Programs $93,684,210 against $92,863,387, **over** by $820,823 or 0.88%; Added Needs $30,387,177 against $31,838,016, **under by $1,450,839 or 4.56%** — the largest single variance in the statement; and Adult Education $866,055 against $968,562, under by $102,507 or 10.58%.

Support Services total $65,808,973 against $65,766,960, over by only $42,013 or 0.06% in aggregate, but with substantial offsetting movements within: Pupil $14,314,979, under by $325,217 (2.22%); Instructional Staff $12,235,753, over by $50,603; General Administration $2,635,585, over by $210,639 (8.69%); School Administration $9,542,563, under by $145,043 (1.50%); Business Services $1,944,031, under by $68,265 (3.39%); Operations $14,402,712, over by $292,052 (2.07%); Pupil Transportation $4,343,960, over by just $4,705 (0.11%); Central Services $3,808,740, under by $47,951 (1.24%); and Athletics and Other $2,580,651, over by $70,491 (2.81%). Community Services $163,171 ran over by $16,106 or 10.95%, and Debt Service $591,746 ran under by $72,754 — coincidentally also 10.95%.

The result is revenues over expenditures of **$2,442,666** against a budgeted $800,259 — a favourable variance of $1,642,407. The pattern is that a modest revenue beat driven by PA-18 combined with a significant underspend in Added Needs instruction to produce a year roughly three times better than the final amendment projected. Read against the June 2024 budget presentation delivered two months earlier, which showed a structural deficit of $(7,370,567) for the same year, the contrast is stark: the reported surplus is real, but it rests on $8.8 million of non-recurring COVID revenue.

The Consolidated Debt Service Funds show revenues of $31,044,282 against $30,860,850 budgeted (Local $30,764,986 against $30,560,850, State $279,296 against $300,000) and expenditures of $30,849,637 against $30,849,638 — within one dollar of budget, comprising Principal $18,745,000 exactly as budgeted, Interest $12,102,812 against $12,102,813, and Other Transactions $1,825 exactly. The surplus is $194,645 against a budgeted $11,212.

The Food Service Fund shows revenues of $6,655,436 against $6,458,707 (Local $448,162, State $4,176,181 against $4,339,916, Federal $2,023,290 against $1,679,000 — over by 21%, Interdistrict $7,803) and expenditures of $6,204,141 against $6,060,793 — Salaries $80,395, Employee Benefits $6,150, Purchased Services $2,707,862 against $2,386,359, Supplies and Materials $3,188,949, Capital Outlay $172,101 against $387,500, Other $17,600, and Transfers Out $31,084 against no budget. The surplus is $451,295 against a budgeted $397,914.

The Troy Career Center Fund shows revenues of $2,660,276 against $2,524,947 budgeted, all federal, and expenditures of $2,606,552 — Salaries $962,083, Employee Benefits $561,789, Purchased Services $781,281, Supplies $11,943, Capital Outlay $3,750, Other $175,375 against a $106,500 budget, Debt Service $110,332. The result is a surplus of $53,724, notable because this fund closes at exactly zero in every other statement in the series — federal revenue exceeded the reimbursable expenditure.

The Community Service Fund shows revenues of $1,963,869 against $1,970,000 and expenditures of $2,190,377 against $2,101,071 — Salaries $739,548 over its $716,531 budget, Employee Benefits $373,679, Purchased Services $899,383 over its $837,800 budget, Supplies $63,678 against $36,000, Capital Outlay $114,089 against $115,000 — for a deficit of $(226,508) against a budgeted $(131,071), a $95,437 adverse variance.

The Troy Preschool Fund shows revenues of $4,177,298 against $4,177,057 — within $241 of budget (Local $2,340,579 over its $2,273,000, State $1,836,719 under its $1,904,057) — and expenditures of $3,770,339 against $3,740,667: Salaries $1,395,289, Employee Benefits $766,027, Purchased Services $835,232 against $771,500, Supplies $197,985, Capital Outlay $80,326, Other $4,916, Debt Service $490,565. The surplus is $406,959 against a budgeted $436,390.

The 2019 Capital Projects Fund shows revenue of $77,114 against $80,000 and capital outlay of $648,619 against a $486,200 budget, with the $220,000 Support Services – Central line unspent, for $(571,505) against a budgeted $(626,200).

The 2023 Capital Projects Fund is the year's most consequential result. Revenue of $10,180,060 against $10,200,000 is essentially fully collected, but expenditures of $17,049,404 against $65,327,399 comprise Purchased Services $195,213 and Capital Outlay $16,854,191 against a $65,327,399 budget — **only 26% spent**. The result is $(6,869,344) against a budgeted $(55,127,399). The roughly $48 million left unspent is precisely what carried forward and restated the fund's opening balance for 2024-25 to $133,553,267, and the pattern would repeat: the following year's Amendment 3 would restate the opening balance up another $44,344,268.

The Sinking Fund shows revenue of $4,892,082 against $4,875,000 and capital outlay of $7,323,438 against a $5,800,000 budget — **126% of budget**, the only fund materially overspent — for a deficit of $(2,431,356) against a budgeted $(925,000).

This is the 2023-24 Final Budget Amendment 3 Resolution, agenda item 6.G. on the June 20, 2024 consent agenda, adopted the same evening as the FY2024-25 appropriation resolution. It covers the General Fund, Food Service Fund, Troy Career Center Fund, Community Service Fund, Preschool Fund, School and Student Activities Fund, Capital Maintenance Fund, 2019 Capital Projects Fund, 2023 Capital Projects Fund, Sinking Fund Capital Projects Fund and Debt Service Funds.

The fund summary reads: General Fund $192,248,490; Food Service $6,060,793; Troy Career Center $2,524,947; Community Service $2,101,071; Troy School District Preschool $3,740,667; Troy School and Student Activities $2,900,000; Debt Service Funds $30,849,638; Capital Maintenance nil; 2019 Capital Projects $706,200; 2023 Capital Projects $65,327,399; and Sinking Fund Capital Projects $5,800,000.

General Fund revenues are amended down $526,839 to $193,048,749: Local up $329,819 to $44,487,819; State down $357,018 to $128,542,649; Federal down $10,214 to $7,900,438; and Incoming Transfers and Other down $489,426 to $12,117,843. The July 1 fund balance holds at $32,620,321, making $225,669,070 available to appropriate.

General Fund expenditures are amended up $2,952,943 to $192,248,490. Instruction rises $1,816,326 to $125,669,965: Basic Programs up $925,147 to $92,863,387; Added Needs up $921,138 to $31,838,016; and Adult and Continuing Education down $29,959 to $968,562. Support Services rise $1,072,590 to $65,766,960: Pupil up $185,609 to $14,640,196; Instructional Staff up $248,989 to $12,185,150; General Administration up $109,683 to $2,424,946; School Administration up $87,189 to $9,687,606; Business Services up $224,297 to $2,012,296; Operations and Maintenance up $11,575 to $14,110,660; Pupil Transportation up $33,460 to $4,339,255; Central Services up $206,046 to $3,856,691; and Athletics down $34,258 to $2,510,160. Community Services rise $3,617 to $147,065 and Debt Service rises $60,410 to $664,500.

Excess revenues over expenditures falls from $4,280,041 to $800,259, a reduction of $3,479,782, with the projected June 30 fund balance falling by the same amount from $36,900,362 to $33,420,580. Note the resolution text carries a small internal inconsistency: the operative clause appropriates "$190,748,491 of the total available to appropriate in the General Fund" while the summary and the expenditure table both show $192,248,490 — the former being the figure from the earlier March presentation.

The Food Service Fund is amended with offsetting revenue movements that leave the total unchanged: State falls $1,000,000 to $4,339,916 while Federal rises $992,000 to $1,679,000 and Local rises $8,000 to $439,791, for total revenue of $6,458,707, identical to before. Expenditure is unchanged at $6,060,793, so the surplus stays at $397,914 and the ending balance at $3,413,126.

The Troy Career Center Fund is amended down $248,853 on both sides to $2,524,947 — Federal down $148,853 to $2,524,947 and the $100,000 State line removed entirely. Community Services expenditure falls $133,853 to $2,524,947 and the $115,000 Debt Service line is eliminated. The fund remains balanced at zero.

The Community Service Fund revenue is unchanged at $1,970,000 and expenditure unchanged at $2,101,071 from the April amendment, but the July 1 fund balance is restated down $131,017 to $2,326,059, carrying the projected June 30 balance down $393,514 to $2,194,988.

The Preschool Fund is amended from Amendment 2 to Amendment 3 with small movements: Local up $10,000 to $2,273,000 with State unchanged at $1,904,057, for total revenue of $4,177,057. Instructional Services rise $25,000 to $2,496,378 with supporting services, community services and debt service all unchanged, for total expenditure of $3,740,667. The surplus narrows $15,000 to $436,390 and the projected ending balance falls $15,000 to $2,320,369.

The School and Student Activities Fund is amended up $100,000 on both sides to $2,900,000, with the July 1 balance restated up $300,441 to $2,446,386 — the prior year having closed better than assumed — carrying the projected June 30 balance up by the same $300,441.

The Debt Service Funds are amended with State revenue up $150,000 to $300,000 and Local unchanged at $30,560,850, for total revenue of $30,860,850. Debt Service expenditure is unchanged at $30,849,638. The result improves from $(138,788) to $11,212, and the projected June 30 balance rises $150,000 to $2,441,910. As with the General Fund, the resolution text carries an inconsistency here: the operative clause appropriates "$38,849,638" where the tables show $30,849,638.

The Capital Maintenance Fund has no revenue and no expenditure in either column, with the balance steady at $672,125.

The 2019 Capital Projects Fund revenue falls $145,000 to $80,000. The July 1 balance is restated up $363,541 to $1,685,663. Facilities Acquisition is cut $1,060,922 to $486,200 while a new Support Services – Central line of $220,000 is added, for total expenditure of $706,200, down $840,922. The projected result improves $695,922 to $(626,200) and the projected June 30 balance rises from zero to $1,059,463.

The 2023 Capital Projects Fund carries by far the largest movements. Local revenue rises $1,500,000 to $10,200,000. The July 1 balance is restated up $433,572 to $188,680,666. On the expenditure side the amendment adds three lines that had no original budget at all — Support Services – Instruction Staff $3,500,000, Pupil Transportation Services $3,927,742, and Support Services – Central $2,260,000 — and raises Facilities Acquisition by $25,639,657 to $55,639,657, for total expenditure of $65,327,399, an increase of $35,327,399. The projected result worsens $33,827,399 to $(55,127,399), and the projected June 30 balance falls $33,393,827 from $166,947,094 to $133,553,267. In the event, as the year-end statement shows, only $17,049,404 of that $65.3 million was actually spent.

The Sinking Fund Capital Projects Fund revenue rises $30,000 to $4,875,000, but the July 1 balance is restated **down** $576,720 to $1,927,354. Facilities Acquisition rises $870,000 to $5,800,000. The projected result worsens $840,000 to $(925,000), and the combined effect of the lower opening balance and higher spending takes the projected June 30 balance down $1,416,720 from $2,419,074 to $1,002,354.

https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.page:
What it is
Agenda item 6.H. on the June 20, 2024 consent agenda — the 2024-25 Budget Appropriation Resolution, adopted the same night as the prior year's final amendment.

Millage rates fixed
18.0 mills on non-homesteads; **2.7936 mills on homesteads and industrial personal property**; 8.7936 mills on commercial personal property; 6.10 mills on all classes for debt retirement; 0.9606 mills on all classes for sinking fund purposes.

The 2.7936 homestead figure is the one the operating millage renewal proposal certified two weeks earlier would quote to voters — "The School District only levied 2.7936 mills on personal residences in 2024" — against the 5.7049-mill ceiling being authorized.

General Fund
Revenues: Local $47,455,345; State $126,436,088; Federal $4,502,005; Incoming Transfers and Other $13,151,085 — total $191,544,523. With a $33,420,580 July 1 balance, $224,965,103 is available to appropriate, of which $195,485,356 is appropriated.

Expenditures: Instruction $128,084,453 (Basic Programs $94,757,497; Added Needs $32,343,750; Adult/Continuing $983,206). Support Services $66,585,319 — Pupil $14,911,509; Instructional Staff $12,379,366; General Administration $2,496,767; School Administration $9,925,447; Business Services $2,031,116; Operations/Maintenance $14,134,448; Pupil Transportation $4,308,072; Central Services $3,877,086; Athletics and Other $2,521,508. Community Services $172,084; Debt Service $477,900; Outgoing Transfers $165,600.

The planned result is a $3,940,833 draw on fund balance — the district budgeting a deficit deliberately, consistent with the "Strategic use of Fund Balance" heading in the June presentation.

Other funds
Food Service $6,398,307; Troy Career Center $2,623,839 balanced; Community Service $2,047,885; Preschool $4,070,508; School and Student Activities $2,900,000; Debt Service Funds $31,709,530 against $31,930,500 of revenue; 2023 Capital Projects $87,600,000 against $6,000,000 of revenue and a $133,553,267 opening balance.

Several operative clauses carry figures inconsistent with their own tables — Capital Maintenance appropriates $300,000 against a nil table, 2019 Capital Projects appropriates $1,547,122 against a $1,000,000 table, and Sinking Fund appropriates $4,700,000 against a $5,000,000 table.
https://media.karpowitsch.org/troysd-boa.verbose:
This is the 2024-25 Budget Appropriation Resolution, agenda item 6.H. on the June 20, 2024 consent agenda of the Troy Board of Education, adopted the same evening as the 2023-24 Final Budget Amendment 3. It is the legally operative act of budget adoption for the year.

General Fund revenues estimated available are Local $47,455,345, State $126,436,088, Federal $4,502,005, and Incoming Transfers and Other $13,151,085, totalling $191,544,523. The estimated fund balance available at July 1 is $33,420,580, making $224,965,103 total available to appropriate, of which $195,485,356 is appropriated.

General Fund expenditures are appropriated as follows. Instruction totals $128,084,453: Basic Programs $94,757,497, Added Needs $32,343,750, and Adult/Continuing Education $983,206. Support Services total $66,585,319: Pupil $14,911,509; Instructional Staff $12,379,366; General Administration $2,496,767; School Administration $9,925,447; Business Services $2,031,116; Operations/Maintenance $14,134,448; Pupil Transportation $4,308,072; Central Services $3,877,086; and Support Services (Athletics and Other) $2,521,508. Community Services are $172,084, Debt Service $477,900, and Outgoing Transfers/Other $165,600.

The appropriation exceeds estimated revenue by $3,940,833 — a deliberately budgeted draw on fund balance rather than a shortfall discovered later. The June 6 budget presentation had framed this under the heading "Strategic use of Fund Balance," alongside Federal Funding, Enrollment, Structural Budget and Staff Alignment.

The millage clause fixes the levy: 18.0 mills on non-homesteads; **2.7936 mills on homesteads and industrial personal property**; 8.7936 mills on commercial personal property; 6.10 mills on all classes of property for debt retirement; and 0.9606 mills on all classes for sinking fund purposes. The 2.7936 homestead figure matters beyond this resolution — the operating millage renewal proposal certified to the November 5, 2024 ballot two weeks earlier cites exactly this number to reassure homeowners that the district levies far less on principal residences than the 5.7049-mill ceiling it was asking voters to authorize.

Among the other funds, the Food Service Fund shows revenues of Local $443,500, State $4,500,000 and Federal $1,750,000, totalling $6,693,500; with a $2,803,943 July 1 balance the total available is $9,497,443, against which $6,398,307 is appropriated for Food Services.

The Troy Career Center Fund shows Federal Sources of $2,623,839 with no state revenue and no beginning balance, all appropriated to Community Services, leaving the fund balanced.

The Community Service Fund shows Local revenue of $2,050,000 with a $2,457,076 beginning balance, $4,507,076 available, and $2,047,885 appropriated to Community Services.

The Troy School District Preschool Fund shows Local $2,275,000 and State $1,921,657, totalling $4,196,657; with a $2,320,369 beginning balance the total available is $6,517,026, against which $4,070,508 is appropriated — Instruction $2,520,830, Supporting Services $596,398, Community Services $350,690 and Debt Service $602,590.

The Troy School and Student Activities Fund shows Local revenue of $2,900,000 with a $2,446,386 beginning balance, $5,346,386 available, and $2,900,000 appropriated to Supporting Services.

The Debt Service Funds show Local revenue of $31,930,500 with a $2,441,910 beginning balance, $34,372,410 available, and $31,709,530 appropriated for debt service — leaving a $220,970 surplus.

The Capital Maintenance Fund shows no revenue, a $645,683 beginning balance and no expenditure in its table, though the operative clause appropriates $300,000. The 2019 Capital Projects Fund shows Local revenue of $60,000 with a $1,059,463 beginning balance, $1,119,463 available, and $1,000,000 of Facilities Acquisition in its table, though the operative clause appropriates $1,547,122. The Sinking Fund Capital Projects Fund shows Local revenue of $5,115,000 with a $1,002,354 beginning balance, $6,117,354 available, and $5,000,000 of Facilities Acquisition in its table, though the operative clause appropriates $4,700,000. These three mismatches between the resolving language and the accompanying schedules appear to be drafting carryovers from an earlier version.

The 2023 Capital Projects Fund shows Local revenue of $6,000,000 with a $133,553,267 beginning balance — the figure restated by the prior year's Amendment 3 — for $139,553,267 available, against which $87,600,000 is appropriated: Support Services – Instruction Staff $3,000,000, Facilities Acquisition $75,000,000, Pupil Transportation Services $4,000,000, Support Services – Central $5,600,000, and a further $12,600,000 line. The $4,000,000 pupil transportation appropriation is the school-bus purchase authorized under the 2022 bond proposal; the following year's Amendment 3 would zero it out entirely.

The resolution closes with the standard control provisions. No Board member or employee shall expend or oblige the expenditure of any funds except pursuant to appropriations made by the Board in keeping with the adopted budgetary policy statement, and changes in appropriated amounts require Board approval. The Superintendent is charged with general supervision of budget execution and shall hold department heads responsible for performance within appropriated amounts. The resolution takes effect immediately.

What it is
Unaudited statements for July 1 – August 31, 2024, presented October 15, 2024. Two months in. Budget columns now reflect the 6/20/24 adopted 2024-25 figures across all funds.

General Fund (2 of 12 months)
- Revenues $9,077,298 of $191,544,523 (4.7%) — Local $9,057,165; State **nil**; Federal **nil**; Interdistrict $20,133
- Expenditures $12,743,671 of $195,485,356 (6.5%) — Instruction $5,202,050; Support Services $7,504,130
- Result $(3,666,373), already close to the budgeted full-year $(3,940,833)

The deficit is a timing artifact: two months of start-up spending against zero state aid, which supplies 66% of the year's revenue and begins arriving in October.

Start-up spending is visible in the detail — Operations $2,376,165, Central Services $1,079,468 (28% of its annual budget in two months), School Administration $1,148,235, and Instructional Staff $1,084,619, against Pupil Transportation at only $123,081.

Debt Service — the new obligation
Revenues $5,535,581 against no expenditures. The budget now shows **Principal $21,415,000** (up from $18,745,000) and Interest $10,292,530 (down from $12,102,813) for total expenditure of $31,709,530 against $31,930,500 of revenue — the 2023 bond series working through the amortization schedule.

Other funds
Food Service: revenues $116,685 against expenditures $87,811, surplus $28,874 — essentially unchanged from July, with school-year operations not yet begun. Troy Career Center: $147,240 balanced, also unchanged. Community Service: revenues $262,149 against expenditures $138,829, surplus $123,320. Preschool: revenues $259,425 against expenditures $247,623, surplus $11,802.

Capital funds
2023 Capital Projects: revenue $1,708,413 against expenditures of $5,762,970 — capital outlay $5,698,507 plus purchased services $64,463 — a $(4,054,557) draw. The budget is now the full $87,600,000 with its component lines: purchased services $2,258,369, capital outlay $84,151,206, outgoing transfers $1,190,425. Sinking Fund: revenue $868,927 against capital outlay $1,433,063. 2019 Capital Projects: revenue $10,781, no expenditure.

These are Troy School District's unaudited statements for July 1 through August 31, 2024 — two months of fiscal 2024-25 — presented to the Board on October 15, 2024. Unlike the July statement, the budget columns now consistently reflect the 2024-25 figures adopted on June 20, 2024.

General Fund revenues total $9,077,298 against $191,544,523 budgeted, 4.7% of plan. By source: Local Sources $9,057,165 of $47,455,345 — 19%, the summer levy settling; State Sources nil of $126,436,088; Federal Sources nil of $4,502,005; and Interdistrict Sources $20,133 of $13,151,085. Two of the four sources have still produced nothing, and state aid — 66% of the year's budgeted revenue — does not begin until October.

General Fund expenditures total $12,743,671 against $195,485,356, 6.5%. Instruction totals $5,202,050 against $128,084,453 — Basic Programs $4,005,192, Added Needs $1,108,944, Adult Education $87,914. Support Services total $7,504,130 against $66,585,319: Pupil $715,780; Instructional Staff $1,084,619; General Administration $333,431; School Administration $1,148,235; Business Services $348,184; Operations $2,376,165; Pupil Transportation $123,081; Central Services $1,079,468; Athletics and Other $295,167. Community Services $23,402 and Debt Service $14,089, with Outgoing Transfers nil.

The result is $(3,666,373) against a budgeted full-year $(3,940,833) — the district has, on paper, already absorbed 93% of the deficit it planned for the entire year in two months. This is entirely a timing artifact of the school-aid calendar and carries no information about the year's outcome; the equivalent point in the prior year showed a comparable pattern before the winter settlement reversed it.

The expenditure detail shows a start-up profile. Central Services at $1,079,468 has consumed 28% of its $3,877,086 annual budget in two months — front-loaded annual software, licensing and technology costs. Operations at $2,376,165 is 17% of budget. Against these, Pupil Transportation at $123,081 is only 2.9% of its $4,308,072 budget, since routes run for barely two weeks of the period.

The Consolidated Debt Service Funds show revenues of $5,535,581 (Local $5,535,581 of $31,650,700, State nil of $279,800) against no expenditures, for a surplus of $5,535,581 against a budgeted $220,970. The budget itself has changed materially from the prior year: **Principal is now $21,415,000** against $18,745,000 in 2023-24, while Interest falls to $10,292,530 from $12,102,813 and Other Transactions to $2,000 from $1,825 — total expenditure of $31,709,530 against total revenue of $31,930,500. The rising principal and falling interest reflect the 2023 bond series moving through its amortization schedule.

The Food Service Fund shows revenues of $116,685 of $6,693,500 (Local $754, State nil, Federal $115,931 unchanged from July) against expenditures of $87,811 of $6,398,307 — Salaries $6,370, Employee Benefits $487, Purchased Services $80,954, all unchanged from July, with supplies, capital outlay, other and transfers out all nil — for a surplus of $28,874. The fund recorded essentially no activity in August; school-year meal operations had not yet begun.

The Troy Career Center Fund shows revenues and expenditures of exactly $147,240 each, every line identical to July — Salaries $70,790, Employee Benefits $41,947, Purchased Services $3,300, Supplies $103, Capital Outlay $1,790, Other $20,099, Debt Service $9,211 — balanced at zero with no August activity recorded.

The Community Service Fund shows revenues of $262,149 of $2,050,000 against expenditures of $138,829 of $2,047,885 — Salaries $81,432, Employee Benefits $38,603, Purchased Services $15,137, Supplies $3,656, Capital Outlay nil — for a surplus of $123,320 against a budgeted $2,115. Summer program revenue continues to run ahead of cost.

The Troy Preschool Fund shows revenues of $259,425 of $4,196,657, all local with state nil, against expenditures of $247,623 of $4,070,508 — Salaries $132,826, Employee Benefits $71,511, Purchased Services $8,580, Supplies $32,636, Capital Outlay $1,590, Other $479, Debt Service nil — for a surplus of $11,802 against a budgeted $126,149.

The 2019 Capital Projects Fund shows revenue of $10,781 against $60,000 budgeted, with no capital outlay against a $1,000,000 budget, for a surplus of $10,781 against a budgeted $(940,000).
